A deliberately strange rule.

The money is intentionally small. The point is whether a simple idea can make 1,000 strangers voluntarily choose to become part of the same experiment.

The transparency rule.

This project should remain understandable without fine print.

No fake purpose

The project does not claim to be charity, fundraising for a cause, or an investment.

No financial promise

Your $1 does not create ownership, profit-sharing, repayment rights, or an expectation of financial return.

No pay-to-rank

A larger payment cannot buy an earlier number or extra visibility.

Privacy first

Names, emails, and personal details are not published without permission.

FAQ

What do I get for $1?

A permanent participant number in the experiment. There is no product, financial return, or promised material reward.

Why exactly $1?

The amount is intentionally trivial. The experiment is about participation, scarcity, and the meaning people attach to joining—not the size of the payment.

Why isn't there a PayPal link?

So you do not need to trust a payment URL sent by a stranger. You can open PayPal yourself and type the project email manually.

Will my name be public?

Not unless you explicitly choose to make it public. The public archive can use participant numbers only.
